topic: The Essence of Calculus: From Motion to Infinity
target_audience: High school students or curious beginners

sections.title: The Problem: How Fast is the Cheetah Moving?
lecture_lines: Average speed is calculated over a time interval.
Instantaneous speed requires a single point in time.
We look at tiny intervals approaching zero.
animations: Create a cheetah icon using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] (#FF8C00) and a ground reference line (#FFFFFF).
Animate the cheetah [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] moving linearly along the ground reference.
Flash a 'distance' label (#FFFFFF) above the moving cheetah [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg].

sections.title: The Bridge: The Concept of Limits
lecture_lines: Limits allow us to approach points precisely.
Zooming in reveals the curve's local slope.
Straight lines approximate curves at microscopic scales.
animations: Draw a sequence of smaller and smaller time intervals (#00CED1) using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microscope.svg] to focus on the detail.
Shrink the interval length toward zero on the screen.
Show a value label (#FFFFFF) converging as intervals shrink, visualized through the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magnifying.svg].

sections.title: Differentiation: Measuring Change
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the rate of change precisely.
The speedometer shows instantaneous speed changes.
The derivative represents the curve's slope.
animations: Plot a smooth curve (#FF4500) representing a position function.
Slide a tangent line (#FFFF00) along the curve dynamically, accompanied by a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg] to indicate velocity.
Flash the slope value (#FFFFFF) changing at the point.

sections.title: Integration: Accumulating the Whole
lecture_lines: Integration reverses the process of differentiation.
We sum infinite tiny rectangles for area.
Total distance is the accumulation of speed.
animations: Draw a shape (#32CD32) and fill it with vertical [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rectangle.svg].
Increase the number of [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rectangle.svg] to fill the area.
Highlight the total area sum (#FFFFFF) beneath the curve using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rectangle.svg].

sections.title: The Fundamental Connection
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
We slice motion and glue it back together.
The fundamental theorem links these two ideas.
animations: Display the derivative [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knife.svg] and integral [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/glue.svg] operators side-by-side.
Animate a transformation showing the inverse relationship.
Flash the equality symbol (#FFFFFF) linking the two processes.
